claims.text: Surface mechanical attrition treatment can create a gradient nanostructured surface layer on a conventional coarse-grained metal.
Introducing a gradient nanostructured surface layer will concurrently improve strength and ductility.
SMAT can produce a nanograined surface with a continuous grain-size gradient extending into the bulk.
The resulting structure consists of surface nanograins transitioning to larger, more ductile grains in the core.
The nanograined surface increases strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
The underlying coarse-grained region retains good ductility.
The grain-size gradient promotes heterogeneous deformation and strain partitioning.
Heterogeneous deformation and strain partitioning permit high strength while maintaining plasticity.
The treatment will increase yield strength relative to untreated coarse-grained metal.
The treatment will maintain or slightly enhance ductility relative to untreated metal.
The expected strength improvement is approximately 20–30% relative to baseline.
A gradient layer that is too shallow may fail to produce the proposed strength–ductility benefit.
Treatment parameters that cause excessive brittleness may prevent the proposed benefit.
Metals prone to premature failure after severe plastic deformation may not exhibit the proposed benefit.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property changes depends on composition, processing parameters, and gradient-layer depth.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis asserts improvement in both strength and ductility, whereas the predicted outcome and falsification rule allow ductility merely to remain unchanged. Thus, the operational success criterion does not require the claimed ductility improvement.
